measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment regarding Acting Public Officials
measures.summary: Would amend the City Charter to state that any reference to the Mayor, Comptroller, Council Member, Common Council President or Council President pro tempore includes a person holding that office in an acting capacity. A person serving in one of these offices on an acting basis would have all the powers and duties of the permanent office.
measures.yesMeans: The Charter is amended to state that officials serving in an acting capacity have all the powers of the permanent office.

measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment to require Charter Revision Commissions Every Ten Years
measures.summary: Would require the Common Council to establish a Charter Revision Commission to formally review the City Charter at least once every ten years. The official abstract notes the Charter has been reviewed by such a commission twice since 1999.
measures.yesMeans: A Charter Revision Commission is required at least every ten years.
measures.noMeans: A Charter Revision Commission is not required every ten years.

measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment empowering Council to fill vacancy if Council President becomes Acting Mayor
measures.summary: Would let the Common Council temporarily fill the district Council seat of the Common Council President if that person becomes Acting Mayor. Under current rules that district seat is left vacant.
measures.yesMeans: The Common Council may temporarily fill the district seat of a Council President who becomes Acting Mayor.
measures.noMeans: The district seat of a Council President who becomes Acting Mayor stays vacant.

measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment to Limit Holdover Terms and to Review Inactive Boards
measures.summary: Would limit members of City boards to serving no more than sixty days after their terms expire. It would also suspend City boards that have been inactive until the Common Council reviews whether they are still needed.
measures.yesMeans: Board members may serve no more than sixty days past the end of their terms, and the Common Council must review inactive City boards.
measures.noMeans: Board members may keep serving after their terms expire, and inactive boards stay in existence.

measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment regarding Mayoral Succession
measures.summary: Would amend section 4-5 of the City Charter to state that if the office of Mayor becomes vacant, the Common Council President becomes Acting Mayor. The President's district Council seat would become temporarily vacant and could be filled by the Common Council.
measures.yesMeans: The Charter states that the Common Council President becomes Acting Mayor if the office of Mayor becomes vacant.

measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment to require public website about City boards and board training
measures.summary: Would require the City to maintain a public website with information about City boards, commissions and other public bodies, including an application to fill vacancies. It would also require orientation and training for new board members.
measures.yesMeans: The City must maintain a website about City boards and provide training for new board members.
measures.noMeans: The website and training are not required.

measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment for creation of temporary task forces
measures.summary: Would allow the Mayor and the Common Council to appoint temporary task forces, for terms of up to two years, to advise them on matters concerning the administration, safety or welfare of the City.
measures.yesMeans: The Mayor and Common Council may appoint temporary task forces.
measures.noMeans: The Mayor and Common Council are not given this power.

measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment on Budget Adoption Procedures
measures.summary: Would require the Mayor to give the proposed budget to the City Comptroller before it goes to the Common Council, and let the Comptroller recommend changes to revenue and expenditure estimates. The Common Council could then lower estimates by a two-thirds vote, or raise an expenditure estimate by a majority vote, based on those recommendations.
measures.yesMeans: The Comptroller gains power to recommend budget estimate changes, and the Common Council may act on them.
measures.noMeans: The current budget powers stay unchanged.

measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment to create an Election Reforms Task Force
measures.summary: Would establish a task force to study election changes for City offices, such as ranked choice voting and open primaries. The task force would make recommendations for possible local law proposals at the November 2028 general election.
measures.yesMeans: An Election Reforms Task Force is established.
measures.noMeans: No Election Reforms Task Force is established.

measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment to Create a Civilian Police Advisory Commission
measures.summary: Would create a Civilian Police Advisory Commission of city residents, effective February 1, 2027. The commission would advise City departments on Buffalo policing policies.
measures.yesMeans: A Civilian Police Advisory Commission is created.
measures.noMeans: No Civilian Police Advisory Commission is created.

measures.title: City of Buffalo Charter Amendment to create a Commission on Human Rights
measures.summary: Would establish a Commission on Human Rights, replacing the current Commission on Citizens' Rights and Community Relations. The new commission would have expanded powers, including making recommendations to the Mayor, Common Council, City departments and the community on human rights protections.
measures.yesMeans: A Commission on Human Rights is established.
measures.noMeans: No Commission on Human Rights is established.
